message.content:
**rs7412 (APOE) – allele frequency in European populations**

| Population group | rs7412 allele (T) frequency | Source |
|------------------|-----------------------------|--------|
| European (EUR) – 1000 Genomes Project | **≈ 0.12 – 0.13** (12–13 %) | 1000 Genomes Phase 3 (European superpopulation) |
| European (non-Finnish) – gnomAD v2.1 | **≈ 0.11 – 0.12** (11–12 %) | gnomAD v2.1 (non‑Finnish European subset) |
| European (Finnish) – gnomAD v2.1 | **≈ 0.08 – 0.09** (8–9 %) | gnomAD v2.1 (Finnish subset) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The rs7412 SNP is one of the two defining variants of the APOE gene (the other being rs429358). The T allele at rs7412 is part of the ε2 haplotype, which is associated with a lower risk of Alzheimer’s disease but a higher risk of type III hyperlipoproteinemia. In most European populations the T allele occurs in roughly 10–13 % of chromosomes, though the exact frequency can vary slightly between sub‑populations (e.g., Finnish vs. non‑Finnish Europeans).

> **How to read the table**  
> - The frequency is expressed as the proportion of chromosomes carrying the T allele out of all chromosomes typed for this SNP.  
> - For example, a frequency of 0.12 means that about 12 % of the alleles in the sampled population are T (the rest are the reference allele, usually C).  

> **Why it matters**  
> Knowing the allele frequency helps researchers estimate the prevalence of the ε2 haplotype in a given population and assess its contribution to disease risk or drug response.

---

### Quick reference

- **rs7412**: SNP in APOE gene (chromosome 19).  
- **Alleles**: Reference (C) vs. alternative (T).  
- **European frequency**: ~12 % (T allele).  
- **Variation**: Slightly lower in Finnish Europeans (~9 %).  

If you need more granular data (e.g., by country or by specific European sub‑groups), let me know and I can pull the latest numbers from gnomAD or the 1000 Genomes Project.
